sections.content: How many people are "secondary education teaching professionals"?

312,535 people

were counted on the census as "secondary education teaching professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the ninth most common occupation reported on the census.

Secondary (and middle school deemed secondary), and sixth form education teaching professionals plan, organise and provide instruction in one or more subjects, including physical education, within a prescribed curriculum.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "secondary education teaching professionals", 16.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "secondary education teaching professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "secondary education teaching professionals" included:

  • customer service managers
  • sales accounts and business development managers
  • early education and childcare services managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "secondary education teaching professionals" there were more women than men (64.4% compared with 35.6%).

This means "secondary education teaching professionals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 35.6% and women made up 64.4% of "secondary education teaching professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "secondary education teaching professionals" included:

  • sales and retail assistants
  • medical and dental technicians
  • customer service occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "secondary education teaching professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "secondary education teaching professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "secondary education teaching professionals", 7.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (83.2% compared with 16.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.6%) than self-employed (2.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
